# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 14
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 14

---

## Consensus Translation

*[Paradise: virgins, martyrs, patriarchs, seraphim. Peter's second intercession.]*

1. There were also those who had preserved the virginity of their body, and they praised God with a great voice.

2. I saw also those who had suffered for righteousness' sake. They were clothed in white garments and had crowns upon their heads, and they praised God with a great voice.

3. I asked: "Where are those who have suffered more than these?"

4. The angel said to me: "God has prepared a more glorious place for those who have kept the virginity of their body and for those who have been pure."

5. I saw also Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and they were there in very great gladness.

6. I saw also the angels of light and the seraphim above them, and a great multitude of the righteous in brilliant white light.

7. I marveled greatly and rejoiced, and I asked: "What is this place, and who are these people in it?"

8. The angel answered: "This is the place prepared for those who suffered for God's sake and for those who fear him."

9. I, Peter, said to my Lord: "Is it not possible for sinners to receive mercy even at the last? For it is written that God is compassionate and merciful and does not desire the death of the sinner."

10. The Lord said to me: "Hear me, Peter. What I told you before, and what you have heard and seen — that is the truth. No one who sins and dies in his sin will be saved.

11. But there will be mercy for some, and some will not be saved; they will go to the place of punishment forever.

12. Those whom I have received from below — them I have delivered — these shall receive mercy through me."

---

## Textual Notes

- **"Preserved the virginity of their body" (v.1):** A category of special honor in early Christian communities. The phrase is technical and deliberate.
- **"Crowns upon their heads" (vv.2, cf. ch.11):** Crowns of glory for the righteous martyrs contrast directly with the crowns of fire worn by corrupt priests in ch.11. The same image serves both reward and punishment.
- **"Abraham and Isaac and Jacob" (v.5):** The three patriarchs as representatives of the righteous dead, echoing Jesus's words in Matt 8:11.
- **"It is written that God is compassionate and merciful" (v.9):** An appeal to Ezek 18:23, 32 or Ps 103:8. Peter grounds his intercession in scripture.
- **"Received from below" (v.12):** Possibly a reference to Christ's descent into Hades (1 Pet 3:19) and the liberation of captives. One of the most debated verses in the APE — does it open a door to universal salvation? SOPHIA presents it without resolution.

---
*SOPHIA synthesis: The paradise vision expands to include the cosmic hierarchy. Peter's second intercession and the Lord's nuanced response (judgment is certain; mercy is real; some are delivered) brings the paradise section to its theological climax.*
